statement_en: In the measure space $([0,1],\mathcal{B}([0,1]),m)$, where $m$ is Lebesgue measure, let $I_n = [0,\frac{1}{n^2}]$. Since $$\sum_{n\geq 1} m(I_n)=\sum_{n\geq 1} \frac{1}{n^2}<\infty,$$ it follows that $m(x\in I_n \text{ i.o. })=0$. In other words, almost every point of $[0,1]$ belongs to only finitely many intervals of the form $I_n = [0,\frac{1}{n^2}]$. In fact, the only point belonging to infinitely many such intervals is $x=0$.
key_techniques: computation of Lebesgue measures of intervals
callout_body: $([0,1],\mathcal{B}([0,1]),m)$是一个测度空间，$m$是Lebesgue测度。假设集合$I_n = [0,\frac{1}{n^2}]$,那么因为$$\sum_{n\geq 1} m(I_n)=\sum_{n\geq 1} \frac{1}{n^2}<\infty$$因此$m(x\in I_n \text{ i.o. })=0$。也就是说，$[0,1]$上几乎所有点都只属于有限多个形如$I_n = [0,\frac{1}{n^2}]$的区间，这很显然。其实这里唯一一个属于无穷多个此类区间的点就只有$x=0$这一个点罢了。
